answer: An AI agent economy resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a cryptographically unique identity anchored in a harbor of verifiable human attestations. Forging trust is costly because an attacker must harvest genuine consent, acting as a cedar of social consensus. Scaling a botnet requires forging a comet of synthetic identities that dissipates under scrutiny. The cost is prohibitive: acquiring thousands of human votes to seize influence demands astronomical capital, neutralizing the attacker.
